results.name: Museo Nacional de Antropología
results.why_it_is_special: Mexico's largest and most-visited museum, housing millions of pre-Hispanic artifacts in a stunning modernist building surrounded by the greenery of Chapultepec Park. It welcomed 5 million guests in 2025.

results.name: Museo Frida Kahlo (Casa Azul)
results.why_it_is_special: The "Blue House" where Frida Kahlo was born, lived, and worked. Visitors can see her art, personal belongings, and the intimate atmosphere of her former home in the quiet, bohemian neighbourhood of Coyoacán.

results.name: Museo Soumaya
results.why_it_is_special: Designed by architect Fernando Romero, this free-admission museum is clad in dazzling silver tiles and houses an extensive collection including works by Rodin and Diego Rivera.

results.name: Museo Tamayo
results.why_it_is_special: A leading contemporary art museum set within Chapultepec Park, showcasing international and Mexican modern art in a striking architectural setting.

results.name: Templo Mayor Museum
results.why_it_is_special: Built on the excavation site of the main temple of the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan, this museum displays discoveries from the heart of the ancient city right in the modern downtown.

results.name: Palacio de Bellas Artes
results.why_it_is_special: Mexico City's most iconic cultural facility, combining Art Nouveau and Art Deco styles. It hosts the National Symphonic Orchestra, National Ballet, National Opera, and National Theater companies, plus major murals by Rivera, Orozco, and Siqueiros.

results.name: Casa Estudio Luis Barragán
results.why_it_is_special: The home and studio of Pritzker Prize–winning architect Luis Barragán (1980 laureate), celebrated for its bold use of colour, masterful play of light and shadow, and sensitivity to landscape. A UNESCO World Heritage Site.

results.name: Biblioteca Vasconcelos
results.why_it_is_special: Often called the "Megabiblioteca," this monumental public library designed by Alberto Kalach (opened 2006) features a soaring, open shelving system and gardens with over 160 endemic plant species — one of Mexico's most striking civic interiors.

results.name: Ciudad Universitaria (UNAM Campus)
results.why_it_is_special: The main campus of the National Autonomous University of Mexico, a UNESCO World Heritage Site master-planned by Mario Pani and Enrique del Moral. Over 60 designers contributed to this "choral" modernist masterpiece, which includes the iconic mosaic-covered Central Library by Juan O'Gorman.

results.name: Mercado de la Merced
results.why_it_is_special: One of the largest and oldest traditional markets in Mexico City, spanning several blocks. It offers staggering quantities of fresh produce, meats, spices, street food (migas, tamales, quesadillas), and even an entire section dedicated to candy.

results.name: Mercado de Coyoacán
results.why_it_is_special: A vibrant neighbourhood market combining traditional Mexican handicrafts, antiques, and renowned food stalls — the tostadas de tinga here are famous across the city.

results.name: Mercado Artesanías La Ciudadela
results.why_it_is_special: The city's premier artisan market, offering handmade textiles, pottery, traditional crafts, and Mexican souvenirs — ideal for finding authentic, locally made goods.

results.name: Mercado Roma
results.why_it_is_special: A modern, curated food hall in the trendy Roma neighbourhood, blending artisanal vendors, craft beer, organic products, upscale street food, and live music — a contemporary take on the traditional Mexican market.

results.name: Mercado de San Juan
results.why_it_is_special: The top stop for gourmands and adventurous eaters, this thriving market in the historic core is known for exotic meats, gourmet ingredients, and high-quality produce.

results.name: Franz Mayer Museum
results.why_it_is_special: Mexico City's leading decorative arts museum, housed in a colonial-era building. It regularly hosts major exhibitions blending art, design, and culture.
